# instance.tokens/v1

A multisite host checks an API token one of its instances issued. `pocketone login` and `pocketone clone` sign in
to the instance (its oauth/v1) and get the instance's own token. Where the host, not the instance, answers deploy/v1
and remote/v1, the host checks that token with this contract, so signing in works the same way on every host.

A service contract ([tokens.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/instance/tokens/v1/tokens.go)), one provider, on the host's scope. It holds no auth of its own: the host
decides what an instance token may do there (for example, only the instance's superusers may deploy).

## Use

```go
tk, ok := tokensv1.Contract.In(host.Scope)       // after the host's seal
res, err := tk.Verify(ctx, tokensv1.Input{Instance: id, Token: token})
switch {
case errors.Is(err, tokensv1.ErrNoInstance):     // not one of this runtime's instances, or it has no API tokens
case err != nil:                                 // the instance failed to start: not a refusal
case !res.Valid:                                 // res.Reason: "invalid" or "expired"
default:                                         // res.Grant: the owner (collection, id) and scopes, as api-tokens/v1 says
}
```

The answer is [api-tokens.verify/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/api-tokens.verify/v1)'s `Result`. A token the instance didn't
issue is `Valid: false`, never an error, so a host can tell a refused token from an instance that won't start.
Verifying may start an instance that isn't running.

## Provide

A runtime that can reach inside its instances provides it on the host scope (`ProvideIn`): look up the instance's
app and ask its api-tokens/v1 (`Verify`), mapping `apitokensv1.ErrInvalid` and `ErrExpired` to `Valid: false`.
A runtime that can't (stock PocketBase images) doesn't provide it.
